_comment: SSOT for DISPATCHABLE models on every transport, host included (the `anthropic` transport was added 2026-09-04; before that this file was external-only): per-transport role resolution, prices, limits, authorization gates. Policy prose home: .claude/skills/orchestration/SKILL.md section 5. The ladder in .claude/reference/model_ladder_evidence.md owns role SEMANTICS and the Anthropic-transport mapping; this file owns per-transport resolution. Model churn is an edit in exactly one of the two, never both. Validate with: python3 .claude/tools/model_registry.py --check

codex._comment: OpenAI Codex, billed against a ChatGPT Plus plan — NOT an OpenAI API key, and unrelated to the failure_archaeology `codex/*` git branches. ONE launcher (2026-08-20): the proxy path, which runs the real `claude` binary against a local proxy translating Anthropic Messages traffic to the Codex backend, so the full .claude harness applies. The former `codex exec` launcher (codex_sidecar.sh) is a retired refusing stub — it passed the prompt as argv (dies on the Windows command-line length limit) and its child loaded none of .claude. Proxy is raine/claude-code-proxy v0.1.35 — caixiaoshun/claudex v1.0.0 was tested and REJECTED: its Anthropic->OpenAI tool-schema conversion emits invalid schemas (widens `required` to every property; adds `type:object` beside an `anyOf`), and all three tool-bearing E2E runs failed while the tools-disabled run passed.

modelAttestation._comment: A proxied child CANNOT report which model served it. Claude Code's system prompt asserts a Claude identity, so the arm parrots it; worse, a run with CCP_CODEX_MODEL forcing gpt-5.6-luna reported `modelUsage: [gpt-5.4-mini]` — the child's own pin, not the served model. Any void-check reading modelUsage mislabels the arm. The proxy's own capture is the only valid attestation.

serverSidePins._comment: Model and effort are forced at the PROXY, not via the child's --model, so a role-name pin cannot silently redirect an arm: this transport's alias surface accepts `opus`/`sonnet`/`haiku`/`fable` and full `claude-*` ids as aliases onto GPT models, inverting DeepSeek's behavior of hard-erroring on them. CCP_CODEX_EFFORT's vocabulary is identical to the sidecar's own -e, so no translation table exists.

opencode._limitsSource: models.dev, the OpenCode team's own catalog (first-party metadata, not a benchmark) - refreshed by scripts/opencode_refresh_models.py. Recorded once here because ONE catalog sourced every row on this transport.
opencode._comment: OpenCode Zen FREE tier (https://opencode.ai/zen) — keyless (`Authorization: Bearer public`; any other unauthenticated key 401s, measured 2026-08-22). ONE shape: the proxy path — Zen's own Anthropic surface (/v1/messages) serves free models TEXT-ONLY (any request carrying `tools` upstream-errors [1210] on every free id tested) while its OpenAI surface (/v1/chat/completions) carries function-calling, streaming and tool loops, verified end-to-end including a real `claude` child completing tool-bearing work. Proxy is LiteLLM (uv tool install 'litellm[proxy]' --with 'fastapi<0.120'; newer fastapi removed get_flat_dependant and this LiteLLM imports it), started PER DISPATCH from a generated config pinning exactly one deployment under the requested id — unknown ids fail routing loudly ('No deployments available'), there is NO alias surface, so unlike the codex transport the child's own modelUsage.canonicalModel IS trustworthy identity evidence. costModel is marginal-usd WITH $0-AUTHORED PRICES because the calls ARE $0 (`cost:"0"` in every Zen response); the legal costModel set has no 'free', and plan-quota would demand a quotaProbe nothing here can satisfy — so costUSD 0.0 in records is measured truth, not the pricing artifact it would be on a priced model. Privacy: Zen documents some free ids as permitted to train on submissions during their free period — check its Privacy section before dispatching proprietary material. ONE row on this transport (muse) is Contributor-Free rather than anonymous-free: it needs a real logged-in-account key (credentialVar below), trains on submissions by design, and 500s under the anonymous `public` bearer — see the muse model row's own comment.

anthropic._comment: The HOST transport, added 2026-09-04. This file's scope deliberately now includes it: an Anthropic session is not the only kind of session, so a non-Anthropic host reaching claude-* needs a launcher and a roster row like every other transport, and `model_registry.py available` should be the ONE answer to 'what can I dispatch to'. The ladder still owns role SEMANTICS (roleSource below) -- these rows assert dispatchability only. No baseUrl: the child talks to Anthropic directly. No credentialFile: the credential is the host's own OAuth on disk at credentialPath, which an env scrub does not touch -- see anthropic_sidecar.sh, which deliberately inverts the scrub's original intent (gotcha_claude_code_entrypoint_leaks_host_auth_to_child) for this one transport.

models._comment: roles emptied 2026-09-04. This row asserted `roles: ["opus"]` while its own effort block said `evidence: unmeasured` -- an unbacked routing assertion, surfaced when _validate began rejecting that pair. The transport is suspended, so nothing routed on it; if DeepSeek returns, this row earns its role from a battery cell like every other, and until then it is dispatchable by alias only (-m pro). The sibling `flash` row keeps its roles: its evidence is `measured`.

The live catalog also carries gpt-5.5, gpt-5.4, gpt-5.4-mini and codex-auto-review (captured 2026-08-19; raine additionally registers `-fast` variants and a `[1m]` long-context suffix); those remain unregistered. terra and sol WERE registered 2026-09-04 and are still UNROUTED -- the rule stands unchanged: a `roles` array is a routing assertion, and nothing measured establishes where terra/sol sit relative to this row, so both carry `roles: []` and are reachable only by explicit alias. Registering an id asserts it is dispatchable; only a benchmark asserts what it is FOR.
models._limitsComment: context_window/max_context_window read from OpenAI's own models cache (~/.codex/models_cache.json, written by the codex CLI from the backend) on 2026-08-20 -- first-party metadata, not a benchmark or a community figure. contextTokens is the DEFAULT window; maxContextTokens is the ceiling the model can be opted into, which nothing in this harness currently requests. Claude Code defaults an unrecognized model to 200000, which UNDER-declares this one by 72K, so a launcher must set CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS from contextTokens rather than accept the default. maxOutputTokens stays null: the 32000 a proxied child reports is Claude Code's own default and the cache states no value, so authoring it would record a client artifact as a model fact.

effort._avoidComment: Empty deliberately. `medium` measured flat, but on T2 alone -- one task is not grounds for a never. `high` is the opposite of avoid: it is the measured pin for thick planning.
effort._evidenceComment: model-effort-v1.0, 16 engagement-verified cells, 2026-08-20 (reference/model_ladder_evidence.md, gpt-5.6-luna section). low: T6 22/22 and T10 18/18 kills, both at ceiling already at the floor pin. max: T2 monotone low->max 41->58/151, and T9 parity refactor 12/20 at low -> 20/20 at max, the battery's largest effort movement. high: T4 11/16->14.5/16 at 3x turns and 6x api. medium: flat on T2, one task only. Never cap turns -- T2 triples api time across its bracket while turns plateau at 99->102, so a cap truncates depth rather than cost.

models._comment: Contributor-Free tier (OpenCode's own docs): trains future Meta models on submissions in exchange for access. 1.2 is retired in favor of 1.3 -- 1.2 401s 'Model is disabled' on every call, key or no key; 1.3 answers cleanly on both. The 500s that looked like an auth/account gate (verified 2026-09-03, ~20+ attempts: curl anon+authed, litellm openai+nvidia_nim providers, raw Node fetch, all failing identically) were NEVER about the key -- see apiMode below, the actual cause. The anonymous `public` bearer also answers fine via /v1/responses (verified), so authTier=gated here is the DOCUMENTED/sanctioned path for this tier's training-consent framing, not a technically-enforced gate -- keep using the real key regardless; it costs nothing and is the account-attributable path Contributor-Free's terms describe. 'gated' means 'the credential must not be the public placeholder' (enforced by opencode_sidecar.sh's explicit check), not a dollar floor: this transport declares no balanceUrl, so sc_gate_balance no-ops regardless of gate.minBalanceUSD -- that field is a schema placeholder (model_registry.py requires a numeric value on every gated row) with no live effect here.
models._rolesComment: Promoted from self-identity-only to sonnet 2026-09-04: scored on model-effort-v1.0 against gpt-5.6-luna's own sonnet-claiming evidence on the same battery -- T3/T5 axes tied, T7/T8 execution within one point or exact, one fabrication each on the T1/T2 citation-grounded tasks (identical count, not an asymmetry). No haiku claim: no scout-shaped evidence exists either way. Same principle as terra/sol's `_comment` above: a benchmark asserts what a model is FOR, and this one now has one.

effort._note: measured at max on 8 cells; one low-effort dispatch exists (completed cleanly) but its arm-patches export never ran, so the code delta is gone with the root and it cannot be scored -- zero comparative low-vs-max evidence exists despite the dispatch. Dispatch at max until a scorable rung comparison does.

models._apiModeComment: muse-spark's Zen backend only answers on the OpenAI Responses surface (/v1/responses) -- every Chat Completions call (/v1/chat/completions, any client: curl, litellm's openai/nvidia_nim providers, raw Node fetch) 500s instantly regardless of headers/streaming/token budget, verified 2026-09-04. opencode's own client succeeds because it calls /v1/responses; there is no known Chat-Completions-side workaround. The launcher reads this field and builds litellm_params.model as 'openai/responses/<id>' instead of 'openai/<id>' -- the litellm prefix that forces the Responses call type end-to-end verified through a live proxy on the Anthropic Messages surface, not just the SDK. A small max_tokens (native Claude Code dispatches never send one) starves the reasoning-token budget on this call type and fails distinctly (`max_output_tokens` error, not a 500) -- unrelated to the apiMode fix itself.
